workstream: WS2 — IRR wiring into scoring + consequence-tier gates (proposal V3-1)
summary: Wires WS1's pure-stdlib agent_eval/reliability.py into the local scoring path: the cross-case stability block computes an auto-selected Krippendorff alpha (error samples = missing ratings) over the per_case stability.values matrix that already persists; pairwise comparison persists the currently-dropped pref_ab/pref_ba verdicts plus a swap-consistency rate and a nominal alpha over repeated-run verdict vectors with errored comparisons treated as missing; detect_regressions gains an opt-in min_alpha gate with the perfect-agreement degenerate carve-out (passes) vs errors/samples:1 unavailability (regression); JudgeConfig gains consequence: exploratory|safety|gating whose tier defaults (0.67/0.70/0.80) are resolved at detection time via a new effective_thresholds() accessor that never mutates config.thresholds (harbor/run.py:329 reads it as a required-judges set); min_alpha is scoped off the Harbor and EvalHub client paths (their aggregations carry no stability data) via include_irr=False; report.py renders the coefficient beside the stability bar labeled "single-judge self-consistency alpha (upper bound on inter-rater reliability)" with metric/n/rationale and no Landis-Koch labels. All 8 mandatory corrections from the V3-1 verdict are incorporated (each is called out in the change specs). All line anchors verified against the working tree at commit 157d917.
depends_on: WS1 — agent_eval/reliability.py with the V3-1 API: krippendorff_alpha(units, level) where units is a list of per-unit rating lists (missing ratings simply absent) and level in {nominal, ordinal, interval}, returning value (float|None) + reason (str|None) + n_units + n_ratings; fleiss_kappa(units) for equal-length (complete-matrix) units; select_irr_metric(n_raters, varying_identity, complete_matrix, scale) -> (metric_name, rationale_string). WS2 deliberately does NOT depend on WS1's degenerate-reason wording: score.py prechecks perfect agreement and insufficiency itself and produces machine-readable reason_code values, so the min_alpha gate never string-matches WS1 output. WS1 rationale strings must not cite 'Sec 6.4' (verdict correction 7: the ordinal-distortion material is Section 5.3) — WS2's adapter appends its own Sec 5.3 citation regardless.

No other workstream dependency. Explicitly out of WS2 scope (other workstreams per docs/paper-validity-analysis.md sequencing): cross-family judge panels (P4), bootstrap CIs, V3-3 validity report section, MLflow metric routing of alpha values (gap 6), Harbor/EvalHub reliability parity (gap 5 — WS2 only scopes the gate off those paths with an explicit notice).

changes.spec: Four additions. (a) JudgeConfig field: add `consequence: str = ""` to the dataclass (insert after `samples: int = 1`, config.py:707) with a docstring noting the P5 tiers, that the coefficient gated is single-judge self-consistency alpha (an upper bound on IRR — Prescription 4 caveat), and that 0.70/0.80 are author-proposed while only 0.67 is literature-backed. (b) Module constants near JudgeConfig: `CONSEQUENCE_LEVELS = ("exploratory", "safety", "gating")`, `CONSEQUENCE_TIER_MIN_ALPHA = {"exploratory": 0.67, "safety": 0.70, "gating": 0.80}`, `THRESHOLD_KEYS = frozenset({"min_mean", "min_pass_rate", "min_win_rate", "max_error_rate", "min_alpha"})`. (c) Constructor-site wiring (VERDICT CORRECTION 8 — explicit kwargs at config.py:1281-1301 silently drop unknown YAML keys): add `consequence=str(j.get("consequence", "") or "")` to the JudgeConfig(...) call. Validation in the existing per-judge loop (config.py:1325-1360): raise ValueError if `jc.consequence` is non-empty and not in CONSEQUENCE_LEVELS (message lists valid values); `warnings.warn(..., stacklevel=2)` when consequence is set and `jc.samples == 1` ("no IRR data will exist; the tier-default min_alpha will fail as unavailable unless --samples >= 2 at run time"); `warnings.warn` when consequence is set on a judge that is never sampled — deterministic: no prompt/prompt_file/llm_rubric and no agent block, and builtin kind != "llm" via the `builtin_judge_kind` already imported at :1323. (d) Thresholds validation at load (config.py:1451, currently raw passthrough): keep `config.thresholds = raw.get("thresholds", {})` but first validate — thresholds must be a mapping (ValueError otherwise); for each judge entry that is a dict, `warnings.warn` for keys not in THRESHOLD_KEYS (catches min_apha typos that today silently never gate); if "min_alpha" present it must be numeric, finite, and <= 1.0 (alpha's maximum) else ValueError. (e) New module-level function + method: `def effective_thresholds(thresholds: dict, judges) -> dict` — returns a COPY (`{k: dict(v) if isinstance(v, dict) else v for k, v in (thresholds or {}).items()}`); for each judge (duck-typed: JudgeConfig via getattr or raw dict via .get, so report.py can pass the raw eval.yaml judges list) with a name and a consequence in CONSEQUENCE_TIER_MIN_ALPHA: `out.setdefault(name, {}).setdefault("min_alpha", tier_default)` — explicit min_alpha always wins; invalid consequence strings in raw dicts are skipped silently (already rejected at EvalConfig load). Method `EvalConfig.effective_thresholds(self)` delegates with `(self.thresholds or {}, self.judges)`. VERDICT CORRECTION 3: this NEVER mutates config.thresholds — harbor/run.py:329 `required = set(config.thresholds or {})` (task-package reuse validation) must see the raw dict unchanged; a test asserts non-mutation.

Six changes (score.py already has the agent_eval symlink and _bootstrap first import at :14 — no convention work needed). (1) IRR adapter. Module constants `IRR_REASON_PERFECT = "perfect_agreement"`, `IRR_REASON_INSUFFICIENT = "insufficient_data"`, `IRR_REASON_UNDEFINED = "undefined"`. `def _irr_level(jc, observed) -> str`: "nominal" when jc.feedback_type == "bool" or all observed values are bool, or values are non-numeric (rate over str(v)); "ordinal" when `_numeric_bounds(jc)` (score.py:868) reports is_int for a judge with a declared score_range, or (no jc/no range) all observed values are ints; "interval" for remaining numerics. `def _compute_irr(units, level, n_raters, complete_matrix) -> dict` returning {metric, level, value, reason_code, reason, n_units (units with >= 2 observed ratings), n_ratings (total observed), n_raters, complete_matrix, rationale, and fleiss_kappa/fleiss_reason only when computed}. Logic: flatten observed; if non-empty and all identical -> value None, reason_code=IRR_REASON_PERFECT, reason="zero variance: every observed rating identical across cases and samples" (VERDICT CORRECTION 1 precondition — computed in score.py, not string-matched from WS1); elif fewer than 2 units have >= 2 observed ratings -> reason_code=IRR_REASON_INSUFFICIENT; else call `agent_eval.reliability.krippendorff_alpha(units, level)` and map a None value to reason_code=IRR_REASON_UNDEFINED with WS1's reason. metric+rationale from `select_irr_metric(n_raters=n_raters, varying_identity=True, complete_matrix=complete_matrix, scale=level)` (Appendix A.1: N resamples of one model = varied-identity pool); ALWAYS append to the rationale: "single-judge self-consistency alpha (upper bound on inter-rater reliability): a self-consistent-but-biased judge passes; single-family panels self-agree spuriously (Prescription 4)" (VERDICT CORRECTION 6) and, when level == ordinal, "exact-match agreement distorts ordinal scales (Section 5.3)" (VERDICT CORRECTION 7 — never cite Sec 6.4). Fleiss companion (P3): only when complete_matrix and level in (nominal, ordinal) and all observed values are bool/int -> `fleiss_kappa(units)`. (2) Cross-case stability block (score.py:1660-1676): keep stable_cases/total_cases exactly as today; replace the scored[0]-only `n_samples` inference (score.py:1668) with `samples_set = {r["stability"].get("samples", 1) for r in scored}` and `n_samples = max(samples_set)`; when n_samples > 1 build `units = [list(r["stability"].get("values") or []) for r in scored]` (values excludes error samples -> errors are missing ratings by construction), `complete = len(samples_set) == 1 and all(len(u) == n_samples for u in units)` (VERDICT CORRECTION 8: per-case len(values) == samples, uniform across cases), look up jc via `{jc.name: jc for jc in config.judges}`, and set `aggregated[name]["stability"]["irr"] = _compute_irr(units, _irr_level(jc, flattened), n_samples, complete)`. Persists automatically: _merge_summary at :2741-2744 strips only the "values" key, so stability.irr lands in summary.yaml judges. (3) Pairwise persistence (compare_runs, score.py:2225-2233): per_case entries gain `"pref_ab": r.pref_ab, "pref_ba": r.pref_ba`; result gains `"swap_consistency"` from new `def _swap_consistency(results) -> dict`: consistent = count of (pref_ab, pref_ba) in {("A","B"), ("B","A"), ("tie","tie")}; errors = results whose winner property is "error" (missing pref or call error); inconsistent = the non-error remainder ((A,A)/(B,B) = position bias, tie/X = partial); rate = consistent/(consistent+inconsistent), None when the denominator is 0. Do NOT change PairwiseResult.winner (:2131-2139) or the wins/ties aggregate — inconsistency stays folded into tie for headline counts (non-breaking), now measurable via swap_consistency. (4) _compute_pairwise_stability (score.py:2236-2271): keep runs/wins counts/stable_cases/agreement_rate/flipped_cases byte-identical in semantics (they remain uncorrected exact agreement over raw winner strings including "error"); ADD `"alpha"`: build per-case vectors mapping winner == "error" or missing to None (VERDICT CORRECTION 5 — the pc.get("winner", "error") pattern at :2250 must not leak "error" into the alpha as a nominal category), units = [[v for v in vec if v is not None] for each case], `alpha = _compute_irr(units, "nominal", n_raters=len(runs), complete_matrix=all(len(u) == len(runs) for u in units))`. (5) detect_regressions (score.py:2516): new signature `def detect_regressions(current_results, thresholds, baseline_results=None, *, pairwise=None, include_irr=True)`. Inside the per-judge loop add a `min_alpha` branch guarded by include_irr: read `irr = (current.get("stability") or {}).get("irr") or {}`; if irr.get("value") is a number and < threshold -> Regression(judge, "alpha", f">= {t}", f"{value:.3f}", detail=f"{metric}/{level}, n_units={n_units} — single-judge self-consistency alpha (upper bound on IRR)"); if value is None and reason_code == IRR_REASON_PERFECT -> NO regression (VERDICT CORRECTION 1: perfect-agreement degenerate passes — a mature all-pass suite must not fail CI); any other None/missing (samples:1, deterministic judge, all-errored, insufficient_data, undefined, or no stability key at all) -> Regression with current "n/a" and detail = irr reason or "alpha unavailable — judge ran with samples: 1, is deterministic, or produced no IRR data" (the established configured-but-unavailable pattern). After the main loop, when include_irr and pairwise is truthy (VERDICT CORRECTION 4 — pairwise lives under summary['pairwise'], not summary['judges'], and a judge literally named 'pairwise' is excluded from load_judges at :735/:744 so the main loop's `current is None: continue` never reaches it): pw_name = pairwise.get("judge"); thr = thresholds.get(pw_name) if pw_name else None; if thr and "min_alpha" in thr, apply the same three-way logic to (pairwise.get("stability") or {}).get("alpha"), metric label "pairwise_alpha". (6) CLI wiring: cmd_judges (:2765-2767) computes `eff = config.effective_thresholds()`, gates on `if eff:` (a consequence-only config with no thresholds block must still gate), calls detect_regressions(current_agg, eff), and prints one stderr note per tier-injected judge ("min_alpha 0.70 injected from consequence: safety — author-proposed tier; only 0.67 is literature-backed"); the per-judge stability print (:2731-2739) appends the alpha ("α=0.71 (krippendorff_alpha/ordinal, n=12)" or "α n/a — perfect agreement"). cmd_regression (:2875) -> detect_regressions(current_agg, config.effective_thresholds(), baseline_agg, pairwise=summary.get("pairwise")). cmd_pairwise (:2781-2853): record `result["judge"] = pairwise_jc.name if pairwise_jc else (args.judge or None)` before _merge_summary; after _merge_summary run `regs = detect_regressions({}, config.effective_thresholds(), pairwise=result)`, print each and sys.exit(1) when non-empty; print the swap-consistency and alpha lines alongside the existing stability print (:2842-2851).

VERDICT CORRECTION 2 (Harbor scoping). At :695 change to `score.detect_regressions(summary["judges"], config.thresholds, include_irr=False)` — build_summary (:266-301) and results.py aggregation (:574-581) produce {mean, pass_rate}-only judge entries with no stability key, so a min_alpha threshold (explicit or tier-default) would otherwise flag every Harbor run as a regression. Keep passing the RAW `config.thresholds` (not effective_thresholds) so consequence tiers never activate on this path and `_validate_task_package_reuse`'s `required = set(config.thresholds or {})` at :329 keeps its exact provenance semantics (VERDICT CORRECTION 3). Immediately before the call, print a one-line stderr notice when the gate is being skipped — i.e. when any thresholds entry is a dict containing "min_alpha" or any config.judges entry has a non-empty consequence: "NOTE: min_alpha/consequence reliability gates skipped — Harbor aggregation carries no per-sample stability data; run the local scoring path for IRR." No other change; _write_report (:447) is covered by the report.py execution_mode scoping (run_meta sets execution_mode="harbor" at :642).

Same scoping as Harbor: the client-side summary from _metrics_to_summary (:55-71) maps each judge to {mean, pass_rate} only — no stability ever. At :216-218 change to `score.detect_regressions(summary["judges"], config.thresholds, include_irr=False)`, keep raw config.thresholds, and print the same skip notice under the same condition (explicit min_alpha or any consequence-tagged judge). run_meta already sets execution_mode="evalhub" (:182), which the report renderer uses for the same scoping.

Rendering + gate parity (report.py already bootstraps and can import agent_eval — :16 and main() imports EvalConfig at :2968). (1) `_detect_regressions(judges, thresholds, pairwise=None, include_irr=True)` (:1478-1487) forwards the new kwargs to score.detect_regressions. (2) New helper `_effective_thresholds(config)` -> `agent_eval.config.effective_thresholds(config.get("thresholds") or {}, config.get("judges") or [])` (raw-dict judges are handled by the duck-typed reader). (3) `_render_scoring_summary(summary, config, baseline_summary=None, run_result=None)` (:1302): thresholds = _effective_thresholds(config) (so a consequence-tagged judge shows its tier bound and FAILs in the Status column exactly when the CLI exits 1); `include_irr = (run_result or {}).get("execution_mode") not in ("harbor", "evalhub")`; the authoritative _breached call (:1308-1310) becomes `_detect_regressions(summary.get("judges", {}), thresholds, pairwise=summary.get("pairwise"), include_irr=include_irr)`; after the stability proportion bar (:1361-1364) append `_irr_badge(jst.get("irr"))`; threshold column (:1385-1393) learns `elif "min_alpha" in thresh: thresh_str = f"≥ α {thresh['min_alpha']}"`; the pairwise summary row (:1442-1472) appends the swap-consistency fraction and, when pw.stability.alpha exists, the same badge. (4) New `_irr_badge(irr) -> str`: empty string for falsy irr; visible text `self-consistency α = 0.71` (or `α n/a — perfect agreement` neutral-styled for reason_code perfect_agreement, `α n/a — <reason_code>` warn-styled otherwise); title tooltip = "single-judge self-consistency alpha (upper bound on inter-rater reliability) — {metric}/{level}, n_units={n_units}, n_ratings={n_ratings}. {rationale} Tier thresholds 0.70/0.80 are author-proposed; only 0.67 is literature-backed." (VERDICT CORRECTION 6). Absolutely no Landis-Koch qualitative labels (no "slight/fair/moderate/substantial/almost perfect") anywhere. Small `.irr-badge` CSS rule matching .stab-label sizing. (5) `_render_regressions(summary, config, run_result=None)` (:1490): same effective-thresholds + pairwise + include_irr threading so the Regressions table shows every breach the CLI exits on (this is the invariant tests/test_threshold_consumers.py enforces). (6) `_render_pairwise` (:1521): add "Swap consistency: {consistent}/{consistent+inconsistent} ({rate:.0%}) position-consistent AB/BA verdict pairs ({errors} errored)" when swap_consistency present, and a "self-consistency α = X (nominal, n={n_units} cases x {n_raters} runs; errored comparisons treated as missing ratings — upper bound on IRR)" line when stability.alpha present. (7) generate_report (:2933-2934): pass run_result into both renderers. Back-compat: all new params default to None/True so existing 2-arg test calls keep passing.

Tag parity with the CLI gate (the file's own stated invariant, :49-66). `_detect_regressions(judges, thresholds, pairwise=None, include_irr=True)` forwards kwargs to the path-loaded score module. At the regressions_detected tag site (~:325-337): compute `eff = config.effective_thresholds()` (config is already an EvalConfig here); replace the `if not config.thresholds:` short-circuit with `if not eff:`; derive `include_irr` from the run directory's run_result.json `execution_mode` (not in ("harbor", "evalhub")) — the run_result is already loaded in this command path for cost/token metrics, otherwise read it best-effort with a default of True; pass `pairwise=summary.get("pairwise")`. Do NOT add alpha MLflow metrics — validity-block MLflow routing is gap 6 / the reporting workstream.

Unit + integration tests for the score.py adapter (imports score via the conftest sys.path entries, pattern of tests/test_score_range_enforcement.py). Unit (_compute_irr): (a) all observed identical -> value None, reason_code == "perfect_agreement"; (b) one unit with >=2 ratings only -> "insufficient_data"; (c) a hand-checkable disagreeing nominal matrix -> float value in [-1, 1] (exact expected value pinned against the WS1 fixture set); (d) monkeypatched agent_eval.reliability.krippendorff_alpha stub asserting the units passed exclude error samples (a case whose stability.values is shorter than samples contributes a short unit — missing, never a placeholder category) and the level argument matches. Level selection (_irr_level): feedback_type bool -> nominal; score_range [1,5] -> ordinal; score_range [0,1] with float feedback -> interval; no-config int values -> ordinal. Completeness (VERDICT CORRECTION 8): scored fixtures where one case has len(values)==2 with samples==3 -> complete_matrix False and no fleiss_kappa key; all-complete uniform bool matrix -> complete True and fleiss_kappa present; hand-built scored list with non-uniform samples (3 and 5) -> complete False, n_raters == 5, no crash (kills the scored[0]-only inference). Integration: score_cases with prebuilt 5-tuples [("q", cycling_scorer, "", "llm", 3)] over 3 tmp case dirs and a matching EvalConfig -> aggregated["q"]["stability"]["irr"] has metric == "krippendorff_alpha", correct n_units, and survives the _merge_summary values-strip (simulate the :2741-2744 dict comprehension and assert irr retained). Rationale: contains "self-consistency" and "upper bound", contains "Section 5.3" when ordinal, contains no "Sec 6.4" and none of the Landis-Koch adjectives.

compare_runs and _compute_pairwise_stability. (a) compare_runs with monkeypatched _call_judge returning scripted (pref_ab, pref_ba) sequences and stubbed load_case_record/_format_outputs_for_pairwise: per_case entries carry pref_ab/pref_ba verbatim; swap_consistency counts (A,B) and (tie,tie) as consistent, (A,A) as inconsistent, an errored case excluded from the rate denominator; all-error run -> rate None. (b) _compute_pairwise_stability over 3 synthetic run dicts where one case has winner "error" in run 2: the alpha block's n_ratings shows the error dropped (missing), while agreement_rate/stable_cases keep today's semantics (that case counts as flipped exactly as before — regression-lock on the legacy fields); all-identical verdict vectors -> alpha.value None with reason_code "perfect_agreement"; mixed verdicts -> numeric nominal alpha. (c) cmd_pairwise-level: monkeypatched compare_runs; asserts summary pairwise block records "judge" (resolved name) and that a configured min_alpha threshold on that judge with a breaching alpha exits 1 while a passing/degenerate one exits 0.

detect_regressions min_alpha semantics, pure-dict fixtures (pattern of tests/test_score_range_enforcement.py:140-200). Rows: (1) stability.irr.value 0.4 < min_alpha 0.7 -> one Regression with metric "alpha"; (2) value 0.85 -> none; (3) value None + reason_code "perfect_agreement" -> NONE (VERDICT CORRECTION 1 carve-out); (4) value None + reason_code "insufficient_data" -> regression; (5) no stability key at all (samples:1 local judge) -> regression with "n/a"; (6) same breach with include_irr=False -> no regression (Harbor scoping contract); (7) pairwise kwarg: thresholds {"pw_judge": {"min_alpha": 0.7}}, pairwise {"judge": "pw_judge", "stability": {"alpha": {...}}} -> gates with metric "pairwise_alpha" for breach/pass/degenerate, and is silent when pairwise has no judge name or the name has no threshold; (8) min_alpha degenerate-pass combined with a min_mean breach on the same judge still yields exactly the min_mean regression; (9) judge absent from current_results (`current is None`) -> continue, no crash.
